rated_messages.input_message: Notice what is triggering your urge. Have understanding and kindness for yourself for feeling this urge. It isn't easy, but can you choose to let it be there without smoking?
Seeing other people smoke is a predictable and unavoidable trigger. Take 5 slow, deep breaths and remind yourself that the urge will pass and that you do not need to smoke.
This craving is just an event. A game. It will pass. The game gets easier the more you let your urge pass without smoking. But, it gets harder every time you give in to the urge and smoke.
Instead of lighting up a cigarette, light a scented candle or burn some incense.
Practice staying in this location without smoking. Just notice your urge. Practicing this will weaken this trigger with time. Just think of it as practice.

Don't let anyone tell you how you should or shouldn't feel today. You feel how you feel and that's it. If you're happy and grateful then enjoy the moment, if you're angry and frustrated, know that this will pass.
Try to avoid seeing other people smoke. It might sound basic but brain see, brain want! If you can, make life easier and avoid the people you used to smoke with for some time where possible.
When you are stressed, it is easy to focus on the things that are going wrong. Take a few moments to focus on 5 things that have gone well or that you are thankful for this week.
When your mind tells you that you will be less stressed after smoking a cigarette, remember that you don't have to listen to that thought. It's just a thought and nothing more.
Even though you are stressed, are you willing to sit with this urge until it passes if will help you break this habit?
